verdicts.decision_note: The freelancer explicitly commits to implementing an ETH wallet-payment option, including the required contract and frontend path, in direct response to the client's request.
First concrete ETH-mint failure: ETH was taken but no NFT was received.
Target-specific implementation claim that updated ETH pricing and buffer logic should allow the swap and mint path to complete.
Post-claim persistence: the next reported ETH mint transaction reverted.
Adds a new concrete transaction and systemic diagnosis: the configured on-chain router was incorrect, causing every ETH mint to revert.
Target-specific implementation claim that a redeployed contract with configurable slippage addresses the ETH-mint failure.
The generic success statement and adjacent payment/refund result do not establish that the NFT was received, so they do not verify the complete ETH mint requirement.
The client accepts migration to a fresh contract and exclusion of old NFTs; this changes contract-migration data semantics rather than the ETH wallet mint behavior.
First concrete full verification: the client reports that the ETH mint completed successfully without an ETH approval step.

missing_event_candidates.description: The freelancer reports a distinct ETH transaction failure caused by actual slippage exceeding the configured limit, immediately before the slippage-related implementation claim.
The client accepts use of the replacement contract with fresh NFT state and exclusion of old-contract NFTs from the active systems.
